# Agents

> **The agent runs inside the server.** The loop that works a run is
> `server/src/agent/loop.ts`: a pass claims the installation, re-arms the waits
> it finds, reads each account's changes, asks the decision turn which rule
> applies, and works a run from the model's own step-by-step choices with the
> budget, the authority guard and the record. The accounts it works are the
> groups the Master holds, and it asks the mail server for them on **every
> pass** — so a group the Master is added to in Stalwart's directory is worked by
> the next pass and one the Master leaves stops being worked, with nothing to
> restart. The supervisor that asks it for a pass is
> `server/src/agent/supervisor.ts`, started by the server's own boot
> (`server/src/index.ts`) with the installation it has just read, and it asks
> again on a pushed change, and every ten seconds as the floor without a working
> stream, thirty with one — an installation
> that has chosen no model, or a Master who works no group, leaves it idle with
> a line in the console instead (said once, when the state begins). The agent's decisions are
> [ADR 0027](docs/adr/0027-the-agents-tools-are-described-and-composable.md) (a
> described catalogue of tools), [0028](docs/adr/0028-what-the-agent-decides-and-what-a-person-decides.md)
> (what it decides and what only a person decides),
> [0029](docs/adr/0029-the-conversation-runs-in-chat-and-mail.md) (one
> conversation in chat and mail), [0030](docs/adr/0030-a-run-is-a-document-and-the-record-is-the-product.md)
> (a run is a document, and the record is the product),
> [0031](docs/adr/0031-a-groups-engagement-is-a-rule-in-prose.md) (a group's
> engagement is a rule in prose),
> [0032](docs/adr/0032-one-agent-per-installation-held-by-a-claim.md) (one claim
> holds the installation's single agent) and
> [0033](docs/adr/0033-the-agents-memory-is-a-graph-it-recalls.md) (the agent's
> memory: a graph of facts it recalls on every call).

The agent's freedom is exactly the first class (ADR 0028); the others are
people's.

| | Class | What it covers | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Reversible, inside the group's account | filing a message, a keyword, a label, a folder, writing, moving or renaming a file, creating an event in the group's own calendar, a draft, a workorder step, a KB proposal, a fact, a question | **The agent** |
| 2 | Irreversible or destructive | destroying a message, a folder or a page, emptying a folder, deleting or overwriting a document, changing or removing a calendar event | **A person, always** |
| 3 | Outward | anything that reaches somebody outside the mandate, `mail.send` above all | **A person's word for exactly that message**, or a rule that declares in its own text that it sends |
| 4 | Beyond the policy | an act the written policy forbids | **Only an installation administrator**, proved by the directory and never by the sentence |
| 5 | The intent | which policy is right, what a workorder should carry, whether a KB change is accepted | **Never the agent**: it proposes, a person approves |

Two standing behaviours hold a step to account: the agent reopens a settled step
when the evidence says it is not settled, carrying who and why; and what it
asserts is its own — a step it settles records the agent as its signer with the
evidence beside it, never a person's name on a thing that person did not do.

## The run is the record

**A run is one document in the group's account** and the whole of the agent's
durable state: which rule or instruction started it and which change woke it, the
plan the model chose — each step, what it waits on and the outcome of each one,
so the record alone says why a step ran and why one did not — what it touched,
what it waits for and the sentence it asked in,
every authorisation with the message it arrived in and the authority given, the
evidence behind its claims, and the budget it has spent — the shape, its parser
and its transitions are `server/src/shared/run.ts`, and where a run lives is
`server/src/agent/runs.ts` (ADR 0030). **A run is capped** at 20 steps, 40 model
calls and five minutes of work, so a model that is stuck ends at a record rather
than looping on the account; a refused answer or a call the account refuses is a
step that ended, and it spends a step, so the cap is what stops a run that keeps
failing. **An ending is said, not only recorded**: a run that
could not finish says so in the group's own conversation with the sentence its

  policy page, the moment and the message.
- **The intent is never the agent's**: which policy is right, what a workorder
  should carry, whether a knowledge change is accepted. It proposes; a person
  approves.

what each step answered, every authorisation with the words it arrived in, what

about to do are written **before** the act. A run ends done, waiting on a person,

  let whole: unknown;

    return { problem: `Not valid JSON${errorDetail(err)}.` };

  if (!isRecord(whole)) return { problem: "The document must be a JSON object." };

      instruction: {
        v: INSTRUCTION_VERSION,
        instruction: whole.instruction,

        surfaces: { ...CHAT_ONLY },
        sends: false,
      },
    };

 * An area is a module of tools with one concern: posta, files, calendario,
 * contatti, conoscenza, workorder, chat, memoria. A run is handed the areas its
 * change and its instruction declare, plus the three every run needs — chat (the
 * interface), conoscenza (the shared library) and memoria (what the installation
 * knows).
 *
 * The **vocabulary** lives here because both tiers use it: the server selects a
 * run's catalogue from it, and a member's client draws the areas an instruction
 * may declare. Which tool belongs to which area, and how a catalogue is selected,
 * is the server's (`agent/areas.ts`) — a client has no catalogue to select.
 */

/** The areas the agent works in. */
export const AREA_NAMES = [
  "mail",
  "files",
  "calendar",
  "contacts",
  "knowledge",
  "workorders",
  "chat",
  "memory",
] as const;

export type AreaName = (typeof AREA_NAMES)[number];

/**
 * How many areas one group's instruction may declare.
 *
 * Three is the ceiling that keeps a turn's catalogue small: an instruction that
 * names five is thirty tools in one answer, which is the failure ADR 0038 exists
 * to undo. A group that needs more writes two instructions' worth of work as two
 * groups, or narrows the one it has.
 */
export const MAX_DECLARED_AREAS = 3;

/** The areas every run gets, whatever its change and instruction say. */
export const TRANSVERSAL_AREAS: readonly AreaName[] = ["chat", "knowledge", "memory"];

/** Whether a name is one of the areas. */
export function isAreaName(name: string): name is AreaName {
  return (AREA_NAMES as readonly string[]).includes(name);
}

/**
 * The area a change on a surface falls in, or null when the surface is not one
 * of the group's (`activity`, the installation's own bookkeeping).
 */
export function areaOfSource(source: string): AreaName | null {
  if (source === "workorder") return "workorders";
  return isAreaName(source) ? source : null;
}

/**
 * What a group declares, or the sentence that refuses it.
 *
 * The declared areas are what an instruction states its group works; a change
 * that lands in an area nobody declared is still worked if its own area is the
 * change's (the change is the trigger, ADR 0038) — this is the ceiling, not the
 * routing.
 */
export function declaredAreas(areas: readonly string[]): {
  areas: readonly AreaName[];
  problem: string | null;
} {
  const known = [...new Set(areas.filter((one): one is AreaName => isAreaName(one)))];
  const unknown = areas.filter((one) => !isAreaName(one));
  if (unknown.length)
    return {
      areas: known,
      problem: `There is no area called ${unknown.map((one) => `"${one}"`).join(", ")}. The areas are: ${AREA_NAMES.join(", ")}.`,
    };
  if (known.length > MAX_DECLARED_AREAS)
    return {
      areas: known,
      problem: `An instruction may declare at most ${MAX_DECLARED_AREAS} areas, and this one declares ${known.length}: ${known.join(", ")}. Split the work into two groups, or narrow what this one does.`,
    };
  return { areas: known, problem: null };
}

/**

 * before the areas existed.
 */
export function selectedAreas(
  declared: readonly AreaName[],
  surfaces: SurfaceMatrix | undefined,
): readonly AreaName[] | null {
  if (!declared.length && !surfaces) return null;
  const held = new Set<AreaName>([...TRANSVERSAL_AREAS, ...declared]);
  if (surfaces) for (const area of areasOfSurfaces(surfaces)) held.add(area);
  return AREA_NAMES.filter((area) => held.has(area));
}

/**
 * The areas a group's surface matrix names, leaving out the ones it turned off.
 *
 * The matrix says where a group works (`chat`, `mail`, `files`, `knowledge`,
 * `workorder`, `calendar`); this says which tools that amounts to. Chat is always
 * there: the conversation is the interface whatever the matrix says.
 */
export function areasOfSurfaces(
  surfaces: SurfaceMatrix | undefined,
): readonly AreaName[] {
  const held = new Set<AreaName>(TRANSVERSAL_AREAS);
  for (const [surface, mode] of Object.entries(surfaces ?? {})) {
    // `off` neither wakes nor writes; `watch` and `ondemand` both belong to a
    // catalogue that may act on them.
    if (mode === "off") continue;
    const area = areaOfSource(surface);
    if (area) held.add(area);
  }
  return AREA_NAMES.filter((area) => held.has(area));
}

/**
 * The catalogue one turn reads: the selected areas' writing tools, every area's
 * reading tools, and the harness's own (`run.read`), which is never a group's
 * business but is always available.
 *
 * Reading is free (`surfaces.ts`: a reading is proof, not an act), so the selection
 * narrows **what a run may change**, never what it may look at. A run whose group
 * declares no surface matrix has nothing to select from and is handed the whole
 * catalogue — the arrangement every run had before the areas existed.
 */
export function catalogueFor<T extends { name: string; writes?: boolean }>(
  catalogue: readonly T[],
  areas: readonly AreaName[] | null,
): readonly T[] {
  if (areas === null) return catalogue;
  return catalogue.filter(
    (tool) => !tool.writes || !isAreaTool(tool.name) || areas.includes(areaOf(tool.name)),
  );
}

/**
 * The account's runs by the change that woke them: one entry per change.
 *
 * A run an instruction started names no rule and no change, and is not an answer
 * to one — nothing here. Two runs of one change cannot be written by this build,
 * and the one a pass can continue is the one still running, so that is the one
 * kept when a hand-written pair of documents says otherwise.
 *
 * shortcut: a change is named by its surface, its kind and its address, which is
 * all the change log hands over — so a document created again at a path a run
 * already answered is read as the change that was answered, not as a new one.
 * Upgrade when an event can name the state it happened at, or the object's own
 * version, which is what tells a recurrence from a replay.
 */
function runsByStart(records: readonly RunRecord[]): Map<string, RunDoc> {
  const byStart = new Map<string, RunDoc>();
  for (const { run } of records) {
    const { woke } = run.startedBy;
    if (!woke) continue;
    const key = woke;
    const held = byStart.get(key);
    if (!held || (held.state !== "running" && run.state === "running"))
      byStart.set(key, run);
  }
  return byStart;
}
/** What an agent that is turned off says, in chat and by mail. */
const OFF_NOTICE = "AI agents are turned off.";

/**
 * What a person is told when their words reached the agent and no rule watches
 * the surface they arrived on.
 *
 * One sentence for every surface. A group with no rule watching the conversation
 * is a group whose agent is not asked to speak there, and the same holds for mail
 * — the live defect was that only the conversation got the sentence, so a message
 * to a group with no mail rule was read and dropped without a word.
 */
function noInstructionNotice(
  surface: "chat" | "mail",
  about: { from?: string | null; subject?: string | null } = {},
): string {
  const where = surface === "mail" ? "mail" : "the conversation";
  const from = about.from ? ` from ${about.from}` : "";
  const subject = about.subject ? ` (“${about.subject}”)` : "";
  return `This group has no instruction naming ${where}, so the message${from}${subject} has woken nothing. An administrator can write one in Administration → AI Agents → Instruction.`;
}

/**
 * The areas one run may use: what its group's instruction declares and what the
 * run's own surface matrix named, plus the transversal three.
 *
 * Two declarations while the matrix is still in the tree: the instruction names
 * the areas, and the matrix says where it may act. A run with neither has nothing
 * to select from and is handed the whole catalogue, which is what every run got
 * before the areas existed.
 */
export function selectedAreas(
  declared: readonly AreaName[],
  surfaces: SurfaceMatrix | undefined,
): readonly AreaName[] | null {
  if (!declared.length && !surfaces) return null;
  const held = new Set<AreaName>([...TRANSVERSAL_AREAS, ...declared]);
  if (surfaces) for (const area of areasOfSurfaces(surfaces)) held.add(area);
  return AREA_NAMES.filter((area) => held.has(area));
}

/**
 * The areas a group's surface matrix names, leaving out the ones it turned off.
 *
 * The matrix says where a group works (`chat`, `mail`, `files`, `knowledge`,
 * `workorder`, `calendar`); this says which areas that amounts to. It adds
 * nothing of its own: the three every run has are `selectedAreas`' business.
 */
function areasOfSurfaces(surfaces: SurfaceMatrix | undefined): readonly AreaName[] {
  const held = new Set<AreaName>();
  for (const [surface, mode] of Object.entries(surfaces ?? {})) {
    // `off` neither wakes nor writes; `watch` and `ondemand` both belong to a
    // catalogue that may act on them.
    if (mode === "off") continue;
    const area = areaOfSource(surface);
    if (area) held.add(area);
  }
  return [...held];
}

Revisione completa fatta sul lavoro intero, e applicata. **`9d70e76`**.

## SSOT — violazioni vere trovate

1. **Due definizioni della stessa unione.** `AccountEventSource` in `agent/accountEvent.ts` elencava a mano `"mail" | "files" | "chat" | "workorder" | "knowledge" | "calendar"`: la stessa unione di `SurfaceName` in `shared/surfaces.ts`. Ora è **`export type AccountEventSource = SurfaceName`**, con il commento che dice perché. Effetto: il cast `event.source as SurfaceName` in `coversChange` è sparito.
2. **Due proprietari della regola "le tre trasversali".** `areasOfSurfaces` le aggiungeva e `selectedAreas` le ri-aggiungeva. Ora le aggiunge **solo** `selectedAreas`; `areasOfSurfaces` è privata e fa una cosa sola (leggere la matrice). Il test passa da `selectedAreas`, che è l'API vera.
3. **Due cache dello stesso documento.** `this.above` (livelli di prosa) e `this.instructions` (documento) leggevano la stessa cosa; il primo era derivabile dal secondo. Resta **una** cache; `proseAbove` compone i due livelli al volo.
4. **Payload morto nella GET.** `/prose` restituiva `surfaces` e `sends`, che nessun lettore usa (il pannello mostra prosa e aree). Togliati: il contratto dice solo ciò che qualcuno legge.

## Affermazioni false corrette (SSOT non è solo codice)

- `accountEvent.ts` spiegava per otto righe che "a rule watches..." — ora l'istruzione.
- `changes.ts`: `runsByStart` ("un run di un'istruzione non nomina regola né cambiamento" — falso: è il contrario), il preavviso ("no rule watches"), la nota sul calendario, la licenza di classe 3 ("a rule must carry"), il commento sul "rule listing", il percorso di risposta ("a rule that watches mail").
- **Parole italiane nel codice** (`posta, calendario, contatti, conoscenza, memoria`) nei due file delle aree — legge del repo violata; ora inglese.

## Cose che ho guardato e **deciso di non toccare**

- `startedBy.rule` e `instruction` in `RunStart`: campi di documenti già scritti, contratto del parser — non ridondanza.
- `proseAbove` **e** `instructionOf` in `ChangesDeps`: sembrano due, ma `proseAbove` è l'unico posto che compone i due livelli (installazione + gruppo); toglierlo sposterebbe la stessa composizione in due chiamanti.
- `CHAT_ONLY` scritto a mano: è protetto dal tipo (`SurfaceMatrix`), quindi aggiungere una superficie rompe la compilazione proprio lì — è una copia che si autodenuncia, non un drift.
- `legacyCleared` + marcatore: ruoli diversi (costo per pass vs garanzia durevole), già documentato.

## Stato

Sette file modificati, tutto committato in `9d70e76`, albero pulito. **Nessun gate eseguito**, come da tua regola: le modifiche sono compilate a mano con `tsc`/Biome durante la revisione, ma nessuna suite è stata lanciata — quindi nessun numero verde nuovo da citare.

## Scenari percorsi

1. **Boot, impianto nuovo** (nessuna istruzione, nessuna regola): claim → per ogni account la clear → `findAppFolder`, marcatore assente, `rules/` assente, **e scrive il marcatore lo stesso**. → **D1**.
2. **Impianto che aveva regole**: la clear cancella `rules/` e `agent/rules.json`, scrive il marcatore; la cancellazione finisce nel batch di cambi *dopo* il cursore e viene filtrata come bookkeeping (`isAgentPath`). Il gruppo però resta **senza istruzione**: non lavora più nulla finché un amministratore non la scrive, e una `instruction.json` v1 viene rifiutata (gap a ogni pass). Conseguenza voluta, ma va detta.
3. **Mail in un gruppo che dichiara mail**: due letture (messaggio + `aboutOf`), **una chiamata di modello** (fatti), un run aperto, `areasOfRun` → mail+chat+knowledge+memory, il catalogo è quello giusto. Corretto.
4. **`done` senza aver fatto nulla**: la guardia conta solo i passi *falliti*; zero passi → `done` accettato. → **D2**, ed è il difetto misurato (67 `done` falsi).
5. **Menzione in un gruppo senza istruzione**: nessuna chiamata di modello, un messaggio di preavviso nel thread. Corretto.
6. **Istruzione con zero aree spuntate**: la matrice è chat-only, quindi il gruppo risponde solo in chat e **tace su mail e files senza dirlo**. → **D3**.
7. **Modifica dell'istruzione a metà pass**: la cache è svuotata all'inizio del pass, quindi vale dal pass dopo. Corretto e documentato.
8. **Riavvio a metà run**: il cursore è un documento, i run si riprendono dal loro documento, il marcatore evita di ripulire due volte. Corretto.
9. **Due account in parallelo**: cache e set sono per account; niente condiviso fuori da claim e summary. Corretto.
10. **Istruzione illeggibile**: `instructionOf` lancia dentro il `try` dell'account → gap, gli altri account proseguono. Corretto.
11. **N cambiamenti nello stesso batch**: `runsByStart(held)` ricostruisce la mappa **per ogni cambiamento**. → **D1** (efficienza: O(N × run)).

## I tre difetti

**D1 — `runsByStart` ricostruita per ogni cambiamento.** L'ho introdotta io nella semplificazione: prima la mappa era costruita una volta e invalidata solo quando un run cambiava stato. Con 50 cambiamenti e 100 run sono 5000 iterazioni per pass, inutili. Correggo ora.

**D2 — un `done` con zero passi è accettato.** Non è una svista: il giudice è in Owed. Ma nella traccia è il primo rischio operativo, perché è *il* difetto che le misure hanno trovato.

**D3 — zero aree spuntate tace.** Il pannello fa spuntare le aree ma non dice che senza nessuna il gruppo lavora solo la conversazione. Una riga di aiuto, e il comportamento smette di essere una trappola.

**D4 — il marcatore si scrive anche quando non c'era niente da cancellare**, quindi il primo pass scrive un documento in ogni account del gruppo. Lo correggo: marcatore solo se `removed.length`.

Applico D1 e D4 e la riga del pannello (D3); D2 lo lascio dichiarato, perché è un lavoro (giudice + eval), non una riga.

```json
{"content":"/**\n * What a tool's answer may not carry into a turn (ADR 0038).\n *\n * A tool reads the group's own account, and somebody may have pasted a password\n * into a document or a message. The answer is somebody else's text, so it is\n * **filtered once, at the door**, rather than trusted: a field named like a\n * credential loses its value before the answer reaches a prompt or the record,\n * and the run says that something was withheld so a reader is not left to wonder\n * why a field is empty.\n *\n * This is a name-based filter, not a secret detector: `{\"password\": \"…\"}` and\n * `{\"apiKey\": \"…\"}` are caught, a key pasted inside a paragraph of prose is not.\n * Upgrade when a document is known to carry one that a name cannot find: the\n * callers are `runTool` in the loop and the decision turn's own reads, and both\n * would take a stricter filter in the same place.\n */\n\n/** The names a value is not allowed to travel under. */\nconst SECRET_NAMES =\n  /^(password|passwd|secret|token|api[-_]?key|authorization|credential|private[-_]?key)$/i;\n\n/** What a field keeps in place of its value. */\nexport const WITHHELD = \"[withheld]\";\n\n/** An answer with its credential-shaped fields emptied, and what was withheld. */\nexport function redactSecrets(value: unknown): { value: unknown; withheld: string[] } {\n  const withheld: string[] = [];\n  const walk = (held: unknown, path: string): unknown => {\n    if (Array.isArray(held)) return held.map((one, at) => walk(one, `${path}[${at}]`));\n    if (!held || typeof held !== \"object\") return held;\n    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n    for (const [key, one] of Object.entries(held as Record<string, unknown>)) {\n      if (SECRET_NAMES.test(key) && typeof one === \"string\" && one.trim()) {\n        out[key] = WITHHELD;\n        withheld.push(path ? `${path}.${key}` : key);\n        continue;\n      }\n      out[key] = walk(one, path ? `${path}.${key}` : key);\n    }\n    return out;\n  };\n  return { value: walk(value, \"\"), withheld };\n}\n","path":"/home/remote/git/gilbert/server/src/agent/redact.ts"}
```

- **The grants bound the act.** A run may do what the instruction declares and the
  authority classes allow, whatever the content asks for; an act outside them is
  refused before it runs, and the refusal is on the record.
- **Anything outward is a draft** a person sends (ADR 0041), so the worst a
  malicious mail can obtain is a draft somebody reads before it leaves.
- **A guardrail that fires ends the run.** Input that tries to make the agent act
  outside its grants, and output that carries a credential, stop the run with the
  ending `refused` (ADR 0030 gains that ending) and a sentence that says which
  check fired — not an out-of-budget, which would blame the clock.

### A tool's answer is filtered before the model sees it

A tool that returns a document can return a password somebody pasted into it, and a
tool that reads the installation can return its own credential. So the tool layer
holds **one filter for every answer**: a field that is a credential, a key or a
session token is removed before the answer reaches the turn, and the run records
that something was withheld. It is the same rule as "secrets are not readable by
the agent", applied at the boundary where an answer is made.

### The common path is a workflow; a plan is the exception

A run of any area set runs three beats, each a step of the document:

18: # nvm bin > ~/.opencode/bin > /usr/local/bin) because a non-login process
19: # does not have nvm's bin on PATH.
20: #
21: # `--server` is a per-subcommand flag in this client build: it is accepted
22: # after a subcommand that declares it, never before the subcommand. Only the
23: # subcommands listed below can target a remote server; the plain TUI form
24: # targets it through the top-level flag.
25: set -euo pipefail
26: 
27: self="$(basename -- "$0")"
28: if [ "$self" = opencode-peer ]; then
29:   peer="${1:?usage: opencode-peer <peer> [opencode args...]}"
30:   shift
31: else
32:   peer="${self#opencode-}"
33: fi
34: 
35: env_file="${OPENCODE_PEER_ENV:-$HOME/.config/opencode/${peer}.env}"
36: if [ ! -r "$env_file" ]; then
37:   echo "opencode-peer: cannot read $env_file" >&2
38:   exit 1
39: fi
40: 
41: set -a
42: # shellcheck disable=SC1090
43: . "$env_file"
44: set +a
45: 
46: var="OPENCODE_$(printf '%s' "$peer" | tr '-' '_' | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')_SERVER"
47: server="${!var:-}"
48: 
49: if [ -z "$server" ]; then
50:   echo "opencode-peer: $var is not set in $env_file" >&2
51:   exit 1
52: fi
53: if [ -z "${OPENCODE_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
54:   echo "opencode-peer: OPENCODE_PASSWORD is empty in $env_file" >&2
55:   exit 1
56: fi
57: 
58: # Resolve the client binary: nvm's bin is not on a non-login PATH.
59: opencode_bin="${OPENCODE_BIN:-$(command -v opencode 2>/dev/null || true)}"
60: if [ -z "$opencode_bin" ]; then
61:   for c in "$HOME"/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/opencode "$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode" /usr/local/bin/opencode; do
62:     if [ -x "$c" ]; then
63:       opencode_bin="$c"
64:       break
65:     fi
66:   done
67: fi
68: if [ -z "$opencode_bin" ]; then
69:   echo "opencode-peer: cannot find the opencode binary (set OPENCODE_BIN)" >&2
70:   exit 1
71: fi
72: 
73: # A `run` carries the working directory as the session Location, and the peer only
74: # accepts a path that exists on its own filesystem: anywhere else the call fails
75: # with "Location not found". `/` is the one path every host has, and a peer's agent
76: # chooses its own place to work, so this is the one directory right for every call.
77: cd /
78: 
79: case "${1:-}" in
80:   api|run|mini|models|stats|reload)
81:     exec "$opencode_bin" "$1" --server "$server" "${@:2}"
82:     ;;
83:   *)
84:     exec "$opencode_bin" --server "$server" "$@"
85:     ;;
86: esac

- `mail.reply` and every outward message **create a draft** and return its id; no
  tool submits. The run records the draft as its outcome and evidence, and its
  ending says it is waiting.
- `startedBy.sends` is the rule's declaration that a draft is wanted, not a licence
  the model reads.
- Before a `done` is believed, a second cheap call is given the ask
  (`startedBy.about`), the plan with each step's state and the `evidence`, and
  answers whether the work covers the ask or names what is missing. A "missing"
  answer sends the run back once with the gap named; the second `done` stands and
  the judge's sentence is written on the ending. A `done` with no evidence is
  refused without spending a call.

### The agent is measured on tasks it has already failed

An evaluation set taken from the run corpus — the message, the promise, the outcome
a person would accept — judged by two measures: **the outcome was accepted** and
**what it cost** (calls, refusals, milliseconds). It is run when a tool, an area or
the prompt changes, on the mock, and is not the release gate. Every live failure
adds a task.

=== plan:
# Plan — ADR 0038 in the tree

Status: **in progress, on branch `agents-reloaded`**. The server and the client
carry the new shape; the eval set and the job-shaped catalogue are still owed.
Each block lands green and on its own.

The gate is the project's own (`npm run check:ci`) at every push, and the measure
is the eval set of ADR 0038 — tasks taken from the runs that failed, judged on
whether the work is accepted and what it cost in calls and refusals.

## Done

1. **The areas exist and select the catalogue.**
   `shared/areas.ts` (the vocabulary both tiers read) and `agent/areas.ts` (which
   tool is in which area, and the selection): a run is handed the areas its
   instruction declares and its matrix names, plus chat, knowledge and memory;
   **reading is free, a write needs its area**. Wired into the turn that chooses,
   with the invariant test that a surface turned off takes its writings out.
2. **One instruction is the document.** `InstructionDoc` v2 — prose, areas, the
   surface matrix, and whether it sends — with the v1 document an installation
   already wrote still read, upgraded in memory. `GET /admin/groups/:name/prose`
   returns it; the `PUT` accepts the areas and refuses one nobody has.
3. **The rules are gone.** `rule.ts`, `rules.ts`, `shared/rule.ts`, their tests
   and their endpoints are deleted. The decision turn no longer names rules: it
   is told the change and answers what the change is about. A change is the
   group's when its area is declared or its surface is `watch`; a run is keyed by
   its change, and a group with no instruction gets a notice in its conversation.
   `prose.ts` carries two levels, not three.
4. **The old documents are cleared once.** `agent/legacy.ts` removes `rules/`
   and `agent/rules.json` from an account, writes `agent/reset-0038.json` so it
   happens once, and touches nothing else — the instruction, the runs, the
   cursors and the memory are the group's present. The loop calls it per account
   before anything reads the account (owner decision 2026-10-22: agents-reloaded
   starts from scratch, no residue).
5. **The client says the new words.** `GroupRules.tsx` and the rules calls are
   gone; `GroupInstruction.tsx` shows the prose and a checkbox per area, under
   Administration → AI Agents → Instruction. The `@gilbert/agent` alias the
   browser no longer needs is removed from both configs, and the six stale i18n
   keys are out of the eleven catalogues.
6. **The documents follow the tree.** `FEATURES.md` and `README.md` describe one
   instruction, the areas, the run keyed by its change and the one-off clear.

- The **eval set** (ADR 0038): the 15–20 tasks taken from the 171 measured runs

- The **judge on `done`** and the guardrails that write `refused` (ADR 0038,
  0030): the record reads and draws `refused`; nothing writes it yet, and a
  credential in a tool's answer is not filtered out of what the model sees.
- The **job-shaped catalogue** (ADR 0038): the tools are still the endpoint
  catalogue under area prefixes; the eight job-shaped tools are not written.

 * An instruction this build cannot use.
 *
 * One that is there but unreadable is a **defect the agent reports**, never a
 * level it silently drops (ADR 0031): the pass fails with this and the next one
 * tries again, which is how the people it belongs to learn that their instruction
 * stopped being carried. The code is what a surface composes its own sentence
 * from.
 */
export class InstructionError extends CodedError {
  constructor(code: string, message: string, status = 502) {
    super(code, message, status, "InstructionError");
  }
}

/** The group's standing instruction, or null when it has written none. */
export async function readInstruction(
  ctx: Ctx,
  accountId: string,
): Promise<InstructionDoc | null> {
  let found: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readAppFileAt>>;
  try {
    found = await readAppFileAt(ctx, accountId, INSTRUCTION_FILE);
  } catch (err) {
    // A document that is there with bytes that do not come back is unreadable,
    // not absent: reading it as absent would carry a call with no group level.
    throw unreadable(errorMessage(err));
  }
  if (!found) return null;
  const parsed = parseInstructionDocumentDetailed(found.text);
  if ("problem" in parsed) throw unreadable(parsed.problem);
  return parsed.instruction;
}

function unreadable(why: string): InstructionError {
  return new InstructionError(
    "instruction_unreadable",
    `The group's instruction at ${INSTRUCTION_FILE} is not readable: ${why} It has been left exactly as it is.`,
  );
}

/**
 * A group's instruction, written through the administration's door (ADR 0038).
 *
 * A group's instruction is decided by an installation administrator (owner
 * decision 2026-10-18), so this tier does not write the group's account itself:
 * it calls the routes under `/api/admin/groups/<name>` and the server writes as
 * the Master, behind the same door as the rest of the administration. That is
 * what makes the decision a boundary rather than a hidden button.
 *
 * The shapes are the server's own (`@gilbert/shared/instruction` and
 * `@gilbert/shared/areas`), the document is validated by the server's parser,
 * and the write is a compare-and-set: the state a read answered is sent back,
 * and a write whose account moved under it is refused with 409.
 */

import type { AreaName } from "@gilbert/shared/areas";
import { apiFetch } from "@/jmap/client";

/** One group's instruction, as the route answers it. */
export interface GroupInstruction {
  instruction: string;
  /** The areas the group works: the whole of what a run may change. */
  areas: AreaName[];
  /** The account's FileNode state the read saw: what a write is conditioned on. */
  state: string;
}

function prosePath(group: string, rest = ""): string {
  return `/api/admin/groups/${encodeURIComponent(group)}/prose${rest}`;
}

/** Read a group's instruction and the areas it works. */
export async function readGroupInstruction(group: string): Promise<GroupInstruction> {
  return await apiFetch<GroupInstruction>(prosePath(group));
}

/** Save the instruction and its areas; an emptied field leaves no document behind. */
export async function saveInstruction(
  group: string,
  text: string,
  areas: readonly AreaName[],
  state?: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await apiFetch(prosePath(group, "/instruction"), {
    method: "PUT",
    body: JSON.stringify({
      instruction: text,
      areas,
      ...(state ? { ifInState: state } : {}),

```ts
/**
 * A credential pasted inside somebody's prose, emptied in place.
 *
 * The field filter cannot see this: a message is one string, and "password:
 * hunter2" is not a field named `password`. The pattern is deliberately narrow —
 * a secret word, a colon or an equals sign, a value with no space — so ordinary
 * prose is left alone. It is a net, not a guarantee, and the limit is the same
 * one the filter declares.
 */
const SECRET_IN_TEXT =
  /\b(password|passwd|secret|token|api[-_]?key|authorization)\b(\s*[:=]\s*)(\S+)/gi;

export function redactText(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(SECRET_IN_TEXT, (_all, name: string, sep: string) => `${name}${sep}${WITHHELD}`);
}
```
